entries.f7905ff6eacd201326ddf49b2ee56e77084adad6: <div sID="gen34107" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="11" osisID="Rev.11" sID="Rev.11"/> <div eID="gen34107" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34108" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen34109" type="x-p"/> In this chapter we have an account, I. Of the measuring—reed given to the apostle, to take the dimensions of the temple, <reference osisRef="Rev.11.1-Rev.11.2">ver. 1, 2</reference>. II. Of the two witnesses of God, <reference osisRef="Rev.11.3-Rev.11.13">ver. 3-13</reference>. III. Of the sounding of the seventh trumpet, and what followed upon it, <reference osisRef="Rev.11.14-Rev.11.19">ver. 14</reference>, &c.
entries.e72a719c208da81705fbf1cbd05cf479545fe393: <div eID="gen34109" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen34108" type="introduction"/> <title type="x-s3">The Measuring of the Temple. (<hi type="small-caps">a. d.</hi> 95.)</title> <div sID="gen34110" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">1</hi> And there was given me a reed like unto a rod: and the angel stood, saying, Rise, and measure the temple of God, and the altar, and them that worship therein. <hi type="super">2</hi> But the court which is without the temple leave out, and measure it not; for it is given unto the Gentiles: and the holy city shall they tread under foot forty <hi type="italic">and</hi> two months. <div eID="gen34110" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34111" type="x-p"/> This prophetical passage about measuring the temple is a plain reference to what we find in Ezekiel's vision, <reference osisRef="Ezek.40.3">Ezek. xl. 3</reference>, &c. But how to understand either the one or the other is not so easy. It should seem the design of measuring the temple in the former case was in order to the rebuilding of it, and that with advantage; the design of this measurement seems to be either, 1. For the preservation of it in those times of public danger and calamity that are here foretold; or, 2. For its trial; that it may be seen how far it agrees with the standard, or pattern, in the mount; or, 3. For its reformation; that what is redundant, deficient, or changed, may be regulated according to the true model. Observe, <div eID="gen34111" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34112" type="x-p"/> I. How much was to be measured. 1. <hi type="italic">The temple;</hi> the gospel church in general, whether it be so built, so constituted, as the gospel rule directs, whether it be too narrow or too large, the door too wide or too strait. 2. <hi type="italic">The altar.</hi> That which was the place of the most solemn acts of worship may be put for religious worship in general; whether the church has the true altars, both as to substance and situation: as to substance, whether they take Christ for their altar, and lay down all their offerings there; and in situation, whether the altar be in the holiest; that is, whether they worship God in the Spirit and in truth. 3. The worshippers too must be measured, whether they make God's glory their end and his word their rule, in all their acts of worship; and whether they come to God with suitable affections, and whether their <hi type="italic">conversation be as becomes the gospel.</hi> <div eID="gen34112" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34113" type="x-p"/> II. What was not to be measured (<reference osisRef="Rev.11.2">v. 2</reference>), and why it should be left out. 1. What was not to be measured: <hi type="italic">The court which is without the temple measure it not.</hi> Some say that Herod, in the additions made to the temple, built an outer court, and called it <hi type="italic">the court of the Gentiles.</hi> Some tell us that Adrian built the city and an outer court, and called it <hi type="italic">Ælia,</hi> and gave it to the Gentiles. 2. Why was not the outer court measured? This was no part of the temple, according to the model either of Solomon or Zerubbabel, and therefore God would have no regard to it. He would not mark it out for preservation; but as it was designed for the Gentiles, to bring pagan ceremonies and customs and to annex them to the gospel churches, so Christ abandoned it to them, to be used as they pleased; and both that and the city were trodden under foot for a certain time—<hi type="italic">forty and two months,</hi> which some would have to be the whole time of the reign of antichrist. Those who worship in the outer court are either such as worship in a false manner or with hypocritical hearts; and these are rejected of God, and will be found among his enemies. 3. From the whole observe, (1.) God will have a temple and an altar in the world, till the end of time. (2.) He has a strict regard to this temple, and observes how every thing is managed in it. (3.) Those who worship in the outer court will be rejected, and only those who worship within the veil accepted. (4.) The holy city, the visible church, is very much trampled upon in the world. But, (5.) The desolations of the church are for a limited time, and for a short time, and she shall be delivered out of all her troubles.
entries.46d27069254f5e93044c5d3d48bc5783a300b7ff: <div eID="gen34113" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Two Witnesses. (<hi type="small-caps">a. d.</hi> 95.)</title> <div sID="gen34114" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">3</hi> And I will give <hi type="italic">power</hi> unto my two witnesses, and they shall prophesy a thousand two hundred <hi type="italic">and</hi> threescore days, clothed in sackcloth. <hi type="super">4</hi> These are the two olive trees, and the two candlesticks standing before the God of the earth. <hi type="super">5</hi> And if any man will hurt them, fire proceedeth out of their mouth, and devoureth their enemies: and if any man will hurt them, he must in this manner be killed. <hi type="super">6</hi> These have power to shut heaven, that it rain not in the days of their prophecy: and have power over waters to turn them to blood, and to smite the earth with all plagues, as often as they will. 7 And when they shall have finished their testimony, the beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit shall make war against them, and shall overcome them, and kill them. <hi type="super">8</hi> And their dead bodies <hi type="italic">shall lie</hi> in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified. <hi type="super">9</hi> And they of the people and kindreds and tongues and nations shall see their dead bodies three days and a half, and shall not suffer their dead bodies to be put in graves. 10 And they that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry, and shall send gifts one to another; because these two prophets tormented them that dwelt on the earth. <hi type="super">11</hi> And after three days and a half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them. <hi type="super">12</hi> And they heard a great voice from heaven saying unto them, Come up hither. And they ascended up to heaven in a cloud; and their enemies beheld them. 13 And the same hour was there a great earthquake, and the tenth part of the city fell, and in the earthquake were slain of men seven thousand: and the remnant were affrighted, and gave glory to the God of heaven. <div eID="gen34114" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34115" type="x-p"/> In this time of treading down, God has reserved to himself his faithful witnesses, who will not fail to attest the truth of his word and worship, and the excellency of his ways. Here observe, <div eID="gen34115" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34116" type="x-p"/> I. The number of these witnesses: it is but a small number and yet it is sufficient. 1. It is but small. Many will own and acknowledge Christ in times of prosperity who will desert and deny him in times of persecution; one witness, when the cause is upon trial, is worth many at other times. 2. It is a sufficient number; for in the mouth of two witnesses every cause shall be established. Christ sent out his disciples two by two, to preach the gospel. Some think these two witnesses are Enoch and Elias, who are to return to the earth for a time: others, the church of the believing Jews and that of the Gentiles: it should rather seem that they are God's eminent faithful ministers, who shall not only continue to profess the Christian religion, but to preach it, in the worst of times. <div eID="gen34116" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34117" type="x-p"/> II. The time of their prophesying, or bearing their testimony for Christ. <hi type="italic">A thousand two hundred and threescore days;</hi> that is (as many think), to the period of the reign of antichrist; and, if the beginning of that interval could be ascertained, this number of prophetic days, taking a day for a year, would give us a prospect when the end shall be. <div eID="gen34117" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34118" type="x-p"/> III. Their habit, and posture: they prophesy in sackcloth, as those that are deeply affected with the low and distressed state of the churches and interest of Christ in the world. <div eID="gen34118" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34119" type="x-p"/> IV. How they were supported and supplied during the discharge of their great and hard work: they stood before the God of the whole earth, and he gave them power to prophesy. He made them to be like Zerubbabel and Joshua, the two olive-trees and candlestick in the vision of Zechariah, <reference osisRef="Zech.4.2">ch. iv. 2</reference>, &c. God gave them the oil of holy zeal, and courage, and strength, and comfort; he made them olive-trees, and their lamps of profession were kept burning by the oil of inward gracious principles, which they received from God. They had oil not only in their lamps, but in their vessels—habits of spiritual life, light, and zeal. <div eID="gen34119" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34120" type="x-p"/> V. Their security and defence during the time of their prophesying: <hi type="italic">If any attempted to hurt them, fire proceeded out of their mouths, and devoured them,</hi> <reference osisRef="Rev.11.5">v. 5</reference>. Some think this alludes to Elias's calling for the fire from heaven, to consume the captains and their companies that came to seize him, <reference osisRef="2Kgs.1.12">2 Kings i. 12</reference>. God promised the prophet Jeremiah (<reference osisRef="Jer.5.14">ch. v. 14</reference>), <hi type="italic">Behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire, and this people shall be wood, and it shall devour them.</hi> By their praying and preaching, and courage in suffering, they shall gall and wound the very hearts and consciences of many of their persecutors, who shall go away self-condemned, and be even terrors to themselves; like Pashur, at the words of the prophet Jeremiah, <reference osisRef="Jer.20.4">ch. xx. 4</reference>. They shall have that free access to God, and that interest in him, that, at their prayers, God will inflict plagues and judgments upon their enemies, as he did on Pharaoh, <hi type="italic">turning their rivers into blood,</hi> and restraining the dews of heaven, shutting heaven up, that no rain shall fall for many days, as he did at the prayers of Elias, <reference osisRef="1Kgs.17.1">1 Kings xvii. 1</reference>. God has ordained his arrows for the persecutors, and is often plaguing them while they are persecuting his people; they find it hard work to <hi type="italic">kick against the pricks.</hi> <div eID="gen34120" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34121" type="x-p"/> VI. The slaying of the witnesses. To make their testimony more strong, they must seal it with their blood. Here observe, 1. The time when they should be killed: <hi type="italic">When they have finished their testimony.</hi> They are immortal, they are invulnerable, till their work be done. Some think it ought to be rendered, <hi type="italic">when they were about to finish their testimony.</hi> When they had prophesied in sackcloth the greatest part of the 1260 years, then they should feel the last effect of antichristian malice. 2. The enemy that should overcome and slay them—<hi type="italic">the beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit.</hi> Antichrist, the great instrument of the devil, should make war against them, not only with the arms of subtle and sophistical learning, but chiefly with open force and violence; and God would permit his enemies to prevail against his witnesses for a time. 3. The barbarous usage of these slain witnesses; the malice of their enemies was not satiated with their blood and death, but pursued even their dead bodies. (1.) They would not allow them a quiet grave; their bodies were cast out in the open street, the high street of Babylon, or in the high road leading to the city. This city is spiritually called Sodom for monstrous wickedness, and Egypt for idolatry and tyranny; and here Christ in his mystical body has suffered more than in any place in the world. (2.) Their dead bodies were insulted by the inhabitants of the earth, and their death was a matter of mirth and joy to the antichristian world, <reference osisRef="Rev.11.10">v. 10</reference>. They were glad to be rid of these witnesses, who by their doctrine and example had teased, terrified, and tormented the consciences of their enemies; these spiritual weapons cut wicked men to the heart, and fill them with the greatest rage and malice against the faithful. <div eID="gen34121" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34122" type="x-p"/> VII. The resurrection of these witnesses, and the consequences thereof. Observe, 1. The time of their rising again; after they had lain dead <hi type="italic">three days and a half</hi> (<reference osisRef="Rev.11.11">v. 11</reference>), a short time in comparison of that in which they had prophesied. Here may be a reference to the resurrection of Christ, who is <hi type="italic">the resurrection and the life. Thy dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise.</hi> Or there may be a reference to the resurrection of Lazarus on the fourth day, when they thought it impossible. God's witnesses may be slain, but they shall rise again: not in their persons, till the general resurrection, but in their successors. God will revive his work, when it seems to be dead in the world. 2. The power by which they were raised: <hi type="italic">The spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet.</hi> God put not only life, but courage into them. God can make the dry bones to life; it is the Spirit of life from God that quickens dead souls, and shall quicken the dead bodies of his people, and his dying interest in the world. 3. The effect of their resurrection upon their enemies: <hi type="italic">Great fear fell upon them.</hi> The reviving of God's work and witnesses will strike terror into the souls of his enemies. Where there is guilt, there is fear; and a persecuting spirit, though cruel, is not a courageous, but a cowardly spirit. Herod feared John the Baptist. <div eID="gen34122" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34123" type="x-p"/> VIII. The ascension of the witnesses into heaven and the consequences thereof, <reference osisRef="Rev.11.12-Rev.11.13">v. 12, 13</reference>. Observe, 1. Their ascension. By heaven we may understand either some more eminent station in the church, the kingdom of grace in this world, or a high place in the kingdom of glory above. The former seems to be the meaning: <hi type="italic">They ascended to heaven in a cloud</hi> (in a figurative, not in a literal sense) <hi type="italic">and their enemies saw them.</hi> It will be no small part of the punishment of persecutors, both in this world and at the great day, that they shall see the faithful servants of God greatly honoured and advanced. To this honour they did not attempt to ascend, till God called them, and said, <hi type="italic">Come up hither.</hi> The Lord's witnesses must wait for their advancement, both in the church and in heaven, till God calls them; they must not be weary of suffering and service, nor too hastily grasp at the reward; but stay till their Master calls them, and then they may gladly ascend to him. 2. The consequences of their ascension—a mighty shock and convulsion in the antichristian empire and the fall of <hi type="italic">a tenth part of the city.</hi> Some refer this to the beginning of the reformation from popery, when many princes and states fell off from their subjection to Rome. This great work met with great opposition; all the western world felt a great concussion, and the antichristian interest received a great blow, and lost a great deal of ground and interest, (1.) By the sword of war, which was then drawn; and many of those who fought under the banner of antichrist were slain by it. (2.) By the sword of the Spirit: <hi type="italic">The fear of God fell upon many.</hi> They were convinced of their errors, superstition, and idolatry; and by true repentance, and embracing the truth, <hi type="italic">they gave glory to the God of heaven.</hi> Thus, when God's work and witnesses revive, the devil's work and witnesses fall before him.
entries.3a32176af8a545371f04ec21b1c5a980808969af: <div eID="gen34123" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Seventh Trumpet. (<hi type="small-caps">a. d.</hi> 95.)</title> <div sID="gen34124" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">14</hi> The second woe is past; <hi type="italic">and,</hi> behold, the third woe cometh quickly. <hi type="super">15</hi> And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become <hi type="italic">the kingdoms</hi> of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever. <hi type="super">16</hi> And the four and twenty elders, which sat before God on their seats, fell upon their faces, and worshipped God, <hi type="super">17</hi> Saying, We give thee thanks, O Lord God Almighty, which art, and wast, and art to come; because thou hast taken to thee thy great power, and hast reigned. <hi type="super">18</hi> And the nations were angry, and thy wrath is come, and the time of the dead, that they should be judged, and that thou shouldest give reward unto thy servants the prophets, and to the saints, and them that fear thy name, small and great; and shouldest destroy them which destroy the earth. <hi type="super">19</hi> And the temple of God was opened in heaven, and there was seen in his temple the ark of his testament: and there were lightnings, and voices, and thunderings, and an earthquake, and great hail. <div eID="gen34124" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34125" type="x-p"/> We have here the sounding of the seventh and last trumpet, which is ushered in by the usual warning and demand of attention: <hi type="italic">The second woe is past, and, behold, the third woe cometh quickly. Then the seventh angel sounded.</hi> This had been suspended for some time, till the apostle had been made acquainted with some intervening occurrences of very great moment, and worthy of his notice and observation. But what he before expected he now heard—the seventh angel sounding. Here observe the effects and consequences of this trumpet, thus sounded. <div eID="gen34125" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34126" type="x-p"/> I. Here were loud and joyful acclamations of the saints and angels in heaven. Observe, 1. The manner of their adorations: they rose from their seats, <hi type="italic">and fell upon their faces, and worshipped God;</hi> they did it with reverence and humility. 2. The matter of their adorations. (1.) They thankfully recognize the right of our God and Saviour to rule and reign over all the world: <hi type="italic">The kingdoms of this world have become the kingdoms of our Lord and of his Christ,</hi> <reference osisRef="Rev.11.15">v. 15</reference>. They were always so in title, both by creation and purchase. (2.) They thankfully observe his actual possession of them, and reign over them; they give him thanks because he had taken to him his great power, asserted his rights, exerted his power, and so turned title into possession. (3.) They rejoice that this his reign shall never end: <hi type="italic">He shall reign for ever and ever,</hi> till all enemies be put under his feet; none shall ever wrest the sceptre out of his hand. <div eID="gen34126" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34127" type="x-p"/> II. Here were angry resentments in the world at these just appearances and actings of the power of God (<reference osisRef="Rev.11.18">v. 18</reference>): <hi type="italic">The nations were angry;</hi> not only had been so, but were so still: their hearts rose up against God; they met his wrath with their own anger. It was a time when God was taking a just revenge upon the enemies of his people, recompensing tribulation to those who had troubled them. It was a time in which he was beginning to reward his people's faithful services and sufferings; and their enemies could not bear it, they fretted against God, and so increased their guilt and hastened their destruction. <div eID="gen34127" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34128" type="x-p"/> III. Another consequence was the opening of the temple of God in heaven. By this may be meant that here is now a more free communication between heaven and earth, prayer and praises more freely and frequently ascending and graces and blessings plentifully descending. But it rather seems to intend the church of God on earth, a heavenly temple. It is an allusion to the various circumstances of things in the time of the first temple. Under idolatrous and wicked princes, it was shut up and neglected; but, under religious and reforming princes, it was opened and frequented. So, during the power of antichrist, the temple of God seemed to be shut up, and was so in a great degree; but now it was opened again. At this opening of it observe, 1. What was seen there: <hi type="italic">the ark of God's testament.</hi> This was in the holy of holies; in this ark the tables of the law were kept. As before Josiah's time the law of God had been lost, but was then found, so in the reign of antichrist God's law was laid aside, and made void by their traditions and decrees; the scriptures were locked up from the people, and they must not look into these divine oracles; now they are opened, now they are brought to the view of all. This was an unspeakable and invaluable privilege; and this, like the ark of the testament, was a token of the presence of God returned to his people, and his favour towards them in Jesus Christ the propitiation. 2. What was heard and felt there: <hi type="italic">Lightnings, voices, thunderings, an earthquake, and great hail.</hi> The great blessing of the reformation was attended with very awful providences; and by terrible things in righteousness God would answer those prayers that were presented in his holy temple, now opened. All the great revolutions of the world are concerted in heaven, and are the answers of the prayers of the saints.  <chapter eID="Rev.11"/> <div eID="gen34128" type="x-p"/>

entries.c625262348f5f0a678f2600be525e1f1fb982384: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19214"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 11</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Rev.11.1-Rev.11.19">Re 11:1-19</reference>. Measurement of the Temple. The Two Witnesses' Testimony:</title> <div sID="gen41825" type="x-p"/> Their Death, Resurrection, and Ascension: The Earthquake: The Third Woe: The Seventh Trumpet Ushers in Christ's Kingdom. Thanksgiving of the Twenty-four Elders.<div eID="gen41825" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41826" type="x-p"/> This eleventh chapter is a compendious summary of, and introduction to, the more detailed prophecies of the same events to come in the twelfth through twentieth chapters. Hence we find anticipatory allusions to the subsequent prophecies; compare <reference osisRef="Rev.11.7">Re 11:7</reference>, "the beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit" (not mentioned before), with the detailed accounts, <reference osisRef="Rev.13.1">Re 13:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.13.11">11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.17.8">17:8</reference>; also <reference osisRef="Rev.11.8">Re 11:8</reference>, "the great city," with <reference osisRef="Rev.14.8">Re 14:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.17.1">17:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.17.5">5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.18.10">18:10</reference>.<div eID="gen41826" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41827" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19214"/><hi type="bold">1. and the angel stood--</hi>omitted in A, Vulgate, and Coptic. Supported by B and Syriac. If it be omitted, the "reed" will, in construction, agree with "saying." So Wordsworth takes it. The reed, the canon of Scripture, the measuring reed of the Church, our rule of faith, speaks. So in <reference osisRef="Rev.16.7">Re 16:7</reference> the altar is personified as speaking (compare Note, see on <reference osisRef="Rev.16.7">Re 16:7</reference>). The Spirit speaks in the canon of Scripture (the word canon is derived from Hebrew, "kaneh," "a reed," the word here used; and John it was who completed the canon). So Victorinus, Aquinas, and Vitringa. "Like a rod," namely, straight: like a rod of iron (<reference osisRef="Rev.2.27">Re 2:27</reference>), unbending, destroying all error, and that "cannot be broken." <reference osisRef="Rev.2.27">Re 2:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.1.8">He 1:8</reference>, Greek, "a rod of straightness," English Version, "a scepter of righteousness"; this is added to guard against it being thought that the reed was one "shaken by the wind" In the abrupt style of the Apocalypse, "saying" is possibly indefinite, put for "one said." Still Wordsworth's view agrees best with Greek. So the ancient commentator, Andreas of Cæsarea, in the end of the fifth century (compare Notes, see on <reference osisRef="Rev.11.3">Re 11:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.11.4">4</reference>).<div eID="gen41827" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41828" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the temple--</hi>Greek, "naon" (as distinguished from the Greek, "hieron," or temple in general), the Holy Place, "the sanctuary."<div eID="gen41828" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41829" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the altar--</hi>of incense; for it alone was in "the sanctuary." (Greek, "naos"). The measurement of the Holy place seems to me to stand parallel to the sealing of the elect of Israel under the sixth seal. God's elect are symbolized by the sanctuary at Jerusalem (<reference osisRef="1Cor.3.16">1Co 3:16</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.3.17">17</reference>, where the same Greek word, "naos," occurs for "temple," as here). Literal Israel in Jerusalem, and with the temple restored (<reference osisRef="Ezek.40.3">Eze 40:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.40.5">5</reference>, where also the temple is measured with the measuring reed, the forty-first, forty-second, forty-third, and forty-fourth chapters), shall stand at the head of the elect Church. The measuring implies at once the exactness of the proportions of the temple to be restored, and the definite completeness (not one being wanting) of the numbers of the Israelite and of the Gentile elections. The literal temple at Jerusalem shall be the typical forerunner of the heavenly Jerusalem, in which there shall be all temple, and no portion exclusively set apart as temple. John's accurately drawing the distinction in subsequent chapters between God's servants and those who bear the mark of the beast, is the way whereby he fulfils the direction here given him to measure the temple. The fact that the temple is distinguished from them that worship therein, favors the view that the spiritual temple, the Jewish and Christian Church, is not exclusively meant, but that the literal temple must also be meant. It shall be rebuilt on the return of the Jews to their land. Antichrist shall there put forward his blasphemous claims. The sealed elect of Israel, the head of the elect Church, alone shall refuse his claims. These shall constitute the true sanctuary which is here measured, that is, accurately marked and kept by God, whereas the rest shall yield to his pretensions. Wordsworth objects that, in the twenty-five passages of the Acts, wherein the Jewish temple is mentioned, it is called hieron, not naos, and so in the apostolic Epistles; but this is simply because no occasion for mentioning the literal Holy Place (Greek, "naos") occurs in Acts and the Epistles; indeed, in <reference osisRef="Acts.7.48">Ac 7:48</reference>, though not directly, there does occur the term, naos, indirectly referring to the Jerusalem temple Holy Place. In addressing Gentile Christians, to whom the literal Jerusalem temple was not familiar, it was to be expected the term, naos, should not be found in the literal, but in the spiritual sense. In <reference osisRef="Rev.11.19">Re 11:19</reference> naos is used in a local sense; compare also <reference osisRef="Rev.14.15">Re 14:15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.14.17">17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.15.5">15:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.15.8">8</reference>. <div eID="gen41829" type="x-p"/>
entries.273cd4980ca6955c62d070403e4a34894f2e6aa5: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19215"/><div sID="gen41830" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19215"/><hi type="bold">2. But--</hi>Greek, "And."<div eID="gen41830" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41831" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the court ... without--</hi>all outside the Holy Place (<reference osisRef="Rev.11.1">Re 11:1</reference>).<div eID="gen41831" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41832" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">leave out--</hi>of thy measurement, literally, "cast out"; reckon as unhallowed.<div eID="gen41832" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41833" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">it--</hi>emphatic. It is not to be measured; whereas the Holy Place is.<div eID="gen41833" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41834" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">given--</hi>by God's appointment.<div eID="gen41834" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41835" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">unto the Gentiles--</hi>In the wider sense, there are meant here "the times of the Gentiles," wherein Jerusalem is "trodden down of the Gentiles," as the parallel, <reference osisRef="Luke.21.24">Lu 21:24</reference>, proves; for the same word is used here [Greek, "patein"], "tread under foot." Compare also <reference osisRef="Ps.79.1">Psa 79:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.63.18">Is 63:18</reference>.<div eID="gen41835" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41836" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">forty ... two months--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Rev.13.5">Re 13:5</reference>). The same period as Daniel's "time, times, and half" (<reference osisRef="Rev.12.14">Re 12:14</reference>); and <reference osisRef="Rev.11.3">Re 11:3</reference>, and <reference osisRef="Rev.12.6">Re 12:6</reference>, the woman a fugitive in the wilderness "a thousand two hundred and threescore days." In the wider sense, we may either adopt the year-day theory of 1260 years (on which, and the papal rule of 1260 years, see on <reference osisRef="Dan.7.25">Da 7:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="Dan.8.14">Da 8:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Dan.12.11">Da 12:11</reference>), or rather, regard the 2300 days (<reference osisRef="Dan.8.14">Da 8:14</reference>), 1335 days (<reference osisRef="Dan.12.11">Da 12:11</reference>, <reference osisRef="Dan.12.12">12</reference>). 1290 days, and 1260 days, as symbolical of the long period of the Gentile times, whether dating from the subversion of the Jewish theocracy at the Babylonian captivity (the kingdom having been never since restored to Israel), or from the last destruction of Jerusalem under Titus, and extending to the restoration of the theocracy at the coming of Him "whose right it is"; the different epochs marked by the 2300, 1335, 1290, and 1260 days, will not be fully cleared up till the grand consummation; but, meanwhile, our duty and privilege urge us to investigate them. Some one of the epochs assigned by many may be right but as yet it is uncertain. The times of the Gentile monarchies during Israel's seven times punishment, will probably, in the narrower sense (<reference osisRef="Rev.11.2">Re 11:2</reference>), be succeeded by the much more restricted times of the personal Antichrist's tyranny in the Holy Land. The long years of papal misrule may be followed by the short time of the man of sin who shall concentrate in himself all the apostasy, persecution, and evil of the various forerunning Antichrists, Antiochus, Mohammed, Popery, just before Christ's advent. His time shall be THE RECAPITULATION and open consummation of the "mystery of iniquity" so long leavening the world. Witnessing churches may be followed by witnessing individuals, the former occupying the longer, the latter, the shorter period. The three and a half (1260 days being three and a half years of three hundred sixty days each, during which the two witnesses prophesy in sackcloth) is the sacred number seven halved, implying the Antichristian world-power's time is broken at best; it answers to the three and a half years' period in which Christ witnessed for the truth, and the Jews, His own people, disowned Him, and the God-opposed world power crucified Him (compare Note, see on <reference osisRef="Dan.9.27">Da 9:27</reference>). The three and a half, in a word, marks the time in which the earthly rules over the heavenly kingdom. It was the duration of Antiochus' treading down of the temple and persecution of faithful Israelites. The resurrection of the witnesses after three and a half days, answers to Christ's resurrection after three days. The world power's times never reach the sacred fulness of seven times three hundred sixty, that is, 2520, though they approach to it in 2300 (<reference osisRef="Dan.8.14">Da 8:14</reference>). The forty-two months answer to Israel's forty-two sojournings (<reference osisRef="Num.33.1-Num.33.50">Nu 33:1-50</reference>) in the wilderness, as contrasted with the sabbatic rest in Canaan: reminding the Church that here, in the world wilderness, she cannot look for her sabbatic rest. Also, three and a half years was the period of the heaven being shut up, and of consequent famine, in Elias' time. Thus, three and a half represented to the Church the idea of toil, pilgrimage, and persecution. <div eID="gen41836" type="x-p"/>
entries.5e061fa0eebacdfbee1e9ec1ad66beacd51d30a0: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19216"/><div sID="gen41837" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19216"/><hi type="bold">3. I will give power--</hi>There is no "power" in the Greek, so that "give" must mean "give commission," or some such word.<div eID="gen41837" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41838" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">my two witnesses--</hi>Greek, "the two witnesses of me." The article implies that the two were well known at least to John.<div eID="gen41838" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41839" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">prophesy--</hi>preach under the inspiration of the Spirit, denouncing judgments against the apostate. They are described by symbol as "the two olive trees" and "the two candlesticks," or lamp-stands, "standing before the God of the earth." The reference is to <reference osisRef="Zech.4.3">Zec 4:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zech.4.12">12</reference>, where two individuals are meant, Joshua and Zerubbabel, who ministered to the Jewish Church, just as the two olive trees emptied the oil out of themselves into the bowl of the candlestick. So in the final apostasy God will raise up two inspired witnesses to minister encouragement to the afflicted, though sealed, remnant. As two candlesticks are mentioned in <reference osisRef="Rev.11.4">Re 11:4</reference>, but only one in <reference osisRef="Zech.4.2">Zec 4:2</reference>, I think the twofold Church, Jewish and Gentile, may be meant by the two candlesticks represented by the two witnesses: just as in <reference osisRef="Rev.7.1-Rev.7.8">Re 7:1-8</reference> there are described first the sealed of Israel, then those of all nations. But see on <reference osisRef="Rev.11.4">Re 11:4</reference>. The actions of the two witnesses are just those of Moses when witnessing for God against Pharaoh (the type of Antichrist, the last and greatest foe of Israel), turning the waters into blood, and smiting with plagues; and of Elijah (the witness for God in an almost universal apostasy of Israel, a remnant of seven thousand, however, being left, as the 144,000 sealed, <reference osisRef="Rev.7.1-Rev.7.8">Re 7:1-8</reference>) causing fire by his word to devour the enemy, and shutting heaven, so that it rained not for three years and six months, the very time (1260 days) during which the two witnesses prophesy. Moreover, the words "witness" and "prophesy" are usually applied to individuals, not to abstractions (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.52.8">Psa 52:8</reference>). De Burgh thinks Elijah and Moses will again appear, as Mal 4:5, 6 seems to imply (compare <reference osisRef="Matt.17.11">Mt 17:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.3.21">Ac 3:21</reference>). Moses and Elijah appeared with Christ at the Transfiguration, which foreshadowed His coming millennial kingdom. As to Moses, compare <reference osisRef="Deut.34.5">De 34:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Deut.34.6">6</reference>; Jude 9. Elias' genius and mode of procedure bears the same relation to the "second" coming of Christ, that John the Baptist's did to the first coming [Bengel]. Many of the early Church thought the two witnesses to be Enoch and Elijah. This would avoid the difficulty of the dying a second time, for these have never yet died; but, perhaps, shall be the witnesses slain. Still, the turning the water to blood, and the plagues (<reference osisRef="Rev.11.6">Re 11:6</reference>), apply best to "Moses (compare <reference osisRef="Rev.15.3">Re 15:3</reference>, the song of Moses"). The transfiguration glory of Moses and Elias was not their permanent resurrection-state, which shall not be till Christ shall come to glorify His saints, for He has precedence before all in rising. An objection to this interpretation is that those blessed departed servants of God would have to submit to death (<reference osisRef="Rev.11.7">Re 11:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.11.8">8</reference>), and this in Moses' case a second time, which <reference osisRef="Heb.9.27">He 9:27</reference> denies. See on <reference osisRef="Zech.4.11">Zec 4:11</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zech.4.12">12</reference>, on the two witnesses as answering to "the two olive trees." The two olive trees are channels of the oil feeding the Church, and symbols of peace. The Holy Spirit is the oil in them. Christ's witnesses, in remarkable times of the Church's history, have generally appeared in pairs: as Moses and Aaron, the inspired civil and religious authorities; Caleb and Joshua; Ezekiel the priest and Daniel the prophet; Zerubbabel and Joshua.<div eID="gen41839" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41840" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in sackcloth--</hi>the garment of prophets, especially when calling people to mortification of their sins, and to repentance. Their very exterior aspect accorded with their teachings: so Elijah, and John who came in His spirit and power. The sackcloth of the witnesses is a catch word linking this episode under the sixth trumpet, with the sun black as sackcloth (in righteous retribution on the apostates who rejected God's witnesses) under the sixth seal (<reference osisRef="Rev.6.12">Re 6:12</reference>). <div eID="gen41840" type="x-p"/>
entries.464ed58b4e9979170537231dfaf73a430095f5ab: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19217"/><div sID="gen41841" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19217"/><hi type="bold">4. standing before the God of the earth--</hi>A, B, C, Vulgate, Syriac, Coptic, and Andreas read "Lord" for "God": so <reference osisRef="Zech.4.14">Zec 4:14</reference>. Ministering to (<reference osisRef="Luke.1.19">Lu 1:19</reference>), and as in the sight of Him, who, though now so widely disowned on "earth," is its rightful King, and shall at last be openly recognized as such (<reference osisRef="Rev.11.15">Re 11:15</reference>). The phrase alludes to <reference osisRef="Zech.4.10">Zec 4:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zech.4.14">14</reference>, "the two anointed ones that stand by the Lord of the whole earth." The article "the" marks this allusion. They are "the two candlesticks," not that they are the Church, the one candlestick, but as its representative light-bearers (Greek, "phosteres," <reference osisRef="Phil.2.15">Php 2:15</reference>), and ministering for its encouragement in a time of apostasy. Wordsworth's view is worth consideration, whether it may not constitute a secondary sense: the two witnesses, the olive trees, are THE TWO Testaments ministering their testimony to the Church of the old dispensation, as well as to that of the new, which explains the two witnesses being called also the two candlesticks (the Old and New Testament churches; the candlestick in <reference osisRef="Zech.4.2">Zec 4:2</reference> is but one as there was then but one Testament, and one Church, the Jewish). The Church in both dispensations has no light in herself, but derives it from the Spirit through the witness of the twofold word, the two olive trees: compare Note, see on <reference osisRef="Rev.11.1">Re 11:1</reference>, which is connected with this, the reed, the Scripture canon, being the measure of the Church: so Primasius [X, p. 314]: the two witnesses preach in sackcloth, marking the ignominious treatment which the word, like Christ Himself, receives from the world. So the twenty-four elders represent the ministers of the two dispensations by the double twelve. But <reference osisRef="Rev.11.7">Re 11:7</reference> proves that primarily the two Testaments cannot be meant; for these shall never be "killed," and never "shall have finished their testimony" till the world is finished. <div eID="gen41841" type="x-p"/>
entries.23203af45b74d72f75f92638ed73e1c634de47cc: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19218"/><div sID="gen41842" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19218"/><hi type="bold">5. will hurt--</hi>Greek, "wishes," or "desires to hurt them."<div eID="gen41842" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41843" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">fire ... devoureth--</hi>(Compare <reference osisRef="Jer.5.14">Jr 5:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.23.29">23:29</reference>).<div eID="gen41843" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41844" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">out of their mouth--</hi>not literally, but God makes their inspired denunciations of judgment to come to pass and devour their enemies.<div eID="gen41844" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41845" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">if any man will hurt them--</hi>twice repeated, to mark the immediate certainty of the accomplishment.<div eID="gen41845" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41846" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in this manner--</hi>so in like manner as he tries to hurt them (compare <reference osisRef="Rev.13.10">Re 13:10</reference>). Retribution in kind. <div eID="gen41846" type="x-p"/>
entries.e2360235f6c602e179f3934d61fc3c2cdf4bd433: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19219"/><div sID="gen41847" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19219"/><hi type="bold">6. These ... power--</hi>Greek, "authorized power."<div eID="gen41847" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41848" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">it rain not--</hi>Greek, "huetos brechee," "rain shower not," literally, "moisten" not (the earth).<div eID="gen41848" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41849" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">smite ... with all plagues--</hi>Greek, "with (literally, 'in') every plague." <div eID="gen41849" type="x-p"/>
entries.b0797ec0d850bd0732377aac20f0df8025392277: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19220"/><div sID="gen41850" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19220"/><hi type="bold">7. finished their testimony--</hi>The same verb is used of Paul's ending his ministry by a violent death.<div eID="gen41850" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41851" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the beast that ascended out of the bottomless pit--</hi>Greek, "the wild beast ... the abyss." This beast was not mentioned before, yet he is introduced as "the beast," because he had already been described by Daniel (<reference osisRef="Dan.7.3">Da 7:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Dan.7.11">11</reference>), and he is fully so in the subsequent part of the Apocalypse, namely, <reference osisRef="Rev.13.1">Re 13:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.17.8">17:8</reference>. Thus, John at once appropriates the Old Testament prophecies; and also, viewing his whole subject at a glance, mentions as familiar things (though not yet so to the reader) objects to be described hereafter by himself. It is a proof of the unity that pervades all Scripture.<div eID="gen41851" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41852" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">make war against them--</hi>alluding to <reference osisRef="Dan.7.21">Da 7:21</reference>, where the same is said of the little horn that sprang up among the ten horns on the fourth beast. <div eID="gen41852" type="x-p"/>
entries.a341b324466ec08bba73c11e9664f347cfc9b665: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19221"/><div sID="gen41853" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19221"/><hi type="bold">8. dead bodies--</hi>So Vulgate, Syriac, and Andreas. But A, B, C, the oldest manuscripts, and Coptic read the singular, "dead body." The two fallen in one cause are considered as one.<div eID="gen41853" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41854" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the great city--</hi>eight times in the Revelation elsewhere used of BABYLON (<reference osisRef="Rev.14.8">Re 14:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.16.19">16:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.17.18">17:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.18.10">18:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.16.18">16, 18</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.19.21">19, 21</reference>). In <reference osisRef="Rev.21.10">Re 21:10</reference> (English Version as to the new Jerusalem), the oldest manuscripts omit "the great" before city, so that it forms no exception. It must, therefore, have an anticipatory reference to the mystical Babylon.<div eID="gen41854" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41855" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">which--</hi>Greek, "the which," namely, "the city which."<div eID="gen41855" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41856" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">spiritually--</hi>in a spiritual sense.<div eID="gen41856" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41857" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Sodom--</hi>The very term applied by <reference osisRef="Isa.1.10">Is 1:10</reference> to apostate Jerusalem (compare <reference osisRef="Ezek.16.48">Eze 16:48</reference>).<div eID="gen41857" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41858" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Egypt--</hi>the nation which the Jews' besetting sin was to lean upon.<div eID="gen41858" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41859" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">where ... Lord was crucified--</hi>This identifies the city as Jerusalem, though the Lord was crucified outside of the city. Eusebius mentions that the scene of Christ's crucifixion was enclosed within the city by Constantine; so it will be probably at the time of the slaying of the witnesses. "The beast [for example, Napoleon and France's efforts] has been long struggling for a footing in Palestine; after his ascent from the bottomless pit he struggles much more" [Bengel]. Some one of the Napoleonic dynasty may obtain that footing, and even be regarded as Messiah by the Jews, in virtue of his restoring them to their own land; and so may prove to be the last Antichrist. The difficulty is, how can Jerusalem be called "the great city," that is, Babylon? By her becoming the world's capital of idolatrous apostasy, such as Babylon originally was, and then Rome has been; just as she is here called also "Sodom and Egypt."<div eID="gen41859" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41860" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">also our--</hi>A, B, C, Origen, Andreas, and others read, "also their." Where their Lord, also, as well as they, was slain. Compare <reference osisRef="Rev.18.24">Re 18:24</reference>, where the blood of ALL slain on earth is said to be found IN Babylon, just as in <reference osisRef="Matt.23.35">Mt 23:35</reference>, Jesus saith that, "upon the Jews and Jerusalem" (Compare <reference osisRef="Matt.23.37">Mt 23:37</reference>, <reference osisRef="Matt.23.38">38</reference>) shall "come ALL the righteous blood shed upon earth"; whence it follows Jerusalem shall be the last capital of the world apostasy, and so receive the last and worst visitation of all the judgments ever inflicted on the apostate world, the earnest of which was given in the Roman destruction of Jerusalem. In the wider sense, in the Church-historical period, the Church being the sanctuary, all outside of it is the world, the great city, wherein all the martyrdoms of saints have taken place. Babylon marks its idolatry, Egypt its tyranny, Sodom its desperate corruption, Jerusalem its pretensions to sanctity on the ground of spiritual privileges, while all the while it is the murderer of Christ in the person of His members. All which is true of Rome. So Vitringa. But in the more definite sense, Jerusalem is regarded, even in Hebrews (<reference osisRef="Heb.13.12-Heb.13.14">He 13:12-14</reference>), as the world city which believers were then to go forth from, in order to "seek one to come." <div eID="gen41860" type="x-p"/>
entries.5063cf66215492f57b2d71a750cc5b8f971dad9b: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19222"/><div sID="gen41861" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19222"/><hi type="bold">9. they--</hi>rather, "(some) of the peoples."<div eID="gen41861" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41862" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">people--</hi>Greek, "peoples."<div eID="gen41862" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41863" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">kindreds--</hi>Greek, "tribes"; all save the elect (whence it is not said, The peoples ... but [some] of the peoples ... , or, some of the peoples ... may refer to those of the nations ..., who at the time shall hold possession of Palestine and Jerusalem).<div eID="gen41863" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41864" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shall see--</hi>So Vulgate, Syriac, and Coptic. But A, B, C, and Andreas, the present, "see," or rather (Greek, "blepousin"), "look upon." The prophetic present.<div eID="gen41864" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41865" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">dead bodies--</hi>So Vulgate, Syriac, and Andreas. But A, B, C, and Coptic, singular, as in <reference osisRef="Rev.11.8">Re 11:8</reference>, "dead body." Three and a half days answer to the three and a half years (see on <reference osisRef="Rev.11.2">Re 11:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.11.3">3</reference>), the half of seven, the full and perfect number.<div eID="gen41865" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41866" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shall not suffer--</hi>so B, Syriac, Coptic, and Andreas. But A, C, and Vulgate read, "do not suffer."<div eID="gen41866" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41867" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in graves--</hi>so Vulgate and Primasius. But B, C, Syriac, Coptic, and Andreas, singular; translate, "into a sepulchre," literally, "a monument." Accordingly, in righteous retribution in kind, the flesh of the Antichristian hosts is not buried, but given to all the fowls in mid-heaven to eat (<reference osisRef="Rev.19.17">Re 19:17</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.18.21">18, 21</reference>). <div eID="gen41867" type="x-p"/>
entries.89e0048d2ee2f69163de9848e9dafcd44c4179db: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19223"/><div sID="gen41868" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19223"/><hi type="bold">10. they that dwell upon ... earth--</hi>those who belong to the earth, as its citizens, not to heaven (<reference osisRef="Rev.3.10">Re 3:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.8.13">8:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.12.12">12:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.13.8">13:8</reference>).<div eID="gen41868" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41869" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shall--</hi>so Vulgate, Syriac, and Coptic. But A, B, and C read the present tense; compare Note, see on <reference osisRef="Rev.11.9">Re 11:9</reference>, on "shall not suffer."<div eID="gen41869" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41870" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">rejoice over them--</hi>The Antichristianity of the last days shall probably be under the name of philosophical enlightenment and civilization, but really man's deification of himself. Fanaticism shall lead Antichrist's followers to exult in having at last seemingly silenced in death their Christian rebukers. Like her Lord, the Church will have her dark passion week followed by the bright resurrection morn. It is a curious historical coincidence that, at the fifth Lateran Council, May 5, 1514, no witness (not even the Moravians who were summoned) testified for the truth, as Huss and Jerome did at Constance; an orator ascended the tribunal before the representatives of papal Christendom, and said, "There is no reclaimant, no opponent." Luther, on October 31, 1517, exactly three and a half years afterwards, posted up his famous theses on the church at Wittenberg. The objection is, the years are years of three hundred sixty-five, not three hundred sixty, days, and so two and a half days are deficient; but still the coincidence is curious; and if this prophecy be allowed other fulfilments, besides the final and literal one under the last Antichrist, this may reasonably be regarded as one.<div eID="gen41870" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41871" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">send gifts one to another--</hi>as was usual at a joyous festival.<div eID="gen41871" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41872" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">tormented them--</hi>namely, with the plagues which they had power to inflict (<reference osisRef="Rev.11.5">Re 11:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.11.6">6</reference>); also, by their testimony against the earthly. <div eID="gen41872" type="x-p"/>
entries.6c114f70dd7a6b2d69c45046e5f8652122a4f518: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19224"/><div sID="gen41873" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19224"/>11. Translate as Greek, "After the three days and an half."<div eID="gen41873" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41874" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the Spirit of life--</hi>the same which breathed life into Israel's dry bones, <reference osisRef="Ezek.37.10">Eze 37:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.37.11">11</reference> (see on <reference osisRef="Ezek.37.10">Eze 37:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.37.11">11</reference>), "Breath came into them." The passage here, as there, is closely connected with Israel's restoration as a nation to political and religious life. Compare also concerning the same, <reference osisRef="Hos.6.2">Ho 6:2</reference>, where Ephraim says, "After two days will He revive us; in the third day He will raise us up, and we shall live in His sight."<div eID="gen41874" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41875" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">into--</hi>so B and Vulgate. But A reads (Greek, "en autois"), "(so as to be) IN them."<div eID="gen41875" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41876" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">stood upon their feet--</hi>the very words in <reference osisRef="Ezek.37.10">Eze 37:10</reference>, which proves the allusion to be to Israel's resurrection, in contrast to "the times of the Gentiles" wherein these "tread under foot the holy city."<div eID="gen41876" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41877" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">great fear--</hi>such as fell on the soldiers guarding Christ's tomb at His resurrection (<reference osisRef="Matt.28.4">Mt 28:4</reference>), when also there was a great earthquake (<reference osisRef="Rev.11.2">Re 11:2</reference>).<div eID="gen41877" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41878" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">saw--</hi>Greek, "beheld." <div eID="gen41878" type="x-p"/>
entries.af416c7d3784e564a856538dbc40d3e2cb410376: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19225"/><div sID="gen41879" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19225"/><hi type="bold">12. they--</hi>so A, C, and Vulgate. But B, Coptic, Syriac, and Andreas read, "I heard."<div eID="gen41879" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41880" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">a cloud--</hi>Greek, "the cloud"; which may be merely the generic expression for what we are familiar with, as we say "the clouds." But I prefer taking the article as definitely alluding to THE cloud which received Jesus at His ascension, <reference osisRef="Acts.1.9">Ac 1:9</reference> (where there is no article, as there is no allusion to a previous cloud, such as there is here). As they resembled Him in their three and a half years' witnessing, their three and a half days lying in death (though not for exactly the same time, nor put in a tomb as He was), so also in their ascension is the translation and transfiguration of the sealed of Israel (<reference osisRef="Rev.7.1-Rev.7.8">Re 7:1-8</reference>), and the elect of all nations, caught up out of the reach of the Antichristian foe. In <reference osisRef="Rev.14.14-Rev.14.16">Re 14:14-16</reference>, He is represented as sitting on a white cloud.<div eID="gen41880" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41881" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">their enemies beheld them--</hi>and were thus openly convicted by God for their unbelief and persecution of His servants; unlike Elijah's ascension formerly, in the sight of friends only. The Church caught up to meet the Lord in the air, and transfigured in body, is justified by her Lord before the world, even as the man-child (Jesus) was "caught up unto God and His throne" from before the dragon standing ready to devour the woman's child as soon as born. <div eID="gen41881" type="x-p"/>
entries.e0e3838cdfba948baec3f8a65ab262f12f14cfaa: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19226"/><div sID="gen41882" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19226"/>13. "In that same hour"; literally, "the hour."<div eID="gen41882" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41883" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">great earthquake--</hi>answering to the "great earthquake" under the sixth seal, just at the approach of the Lord (<reference osisRef="Rev.6.12">Re 6:12</reference>). Christ was delivered unto His enemies on the fifth day of the week, and on the sixth was crucified, and on the sabbath rested; so it is under the sixth seal and sixth trumpet that the last suffering of the Church, begun under the fifth seal and trumpet, is to be consummated, before she enters on her seventh day of eternal sabbath. Six is the number of the world power's greatest triumph, but at the same time verges on seven, the divine number, when its utter destruction takes place. Compare "666" in <reference osisRef="Rev.13.18">Re 13:18</reference>, "the number of the beast."<div eID="gen41883" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41884" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">tenth part of the city fell--</hi>that is, of "the great city" (<reference osisRef="Rev.16.19">Re 16:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.14.2">Zec 14:2</reference>). Ten is the number of the world kingdoms (<reference osisRef="Rev.17.10-Rev.17.12">Re 17:10-12</reference>), and the beast's horns (<reference osisRef="Rev.13.1">Re 13:1</reference>), and the dragon's (<reference osisRef="Rev.12.3">Re 12:3</reference>). Thus, in the Church-historical view, it is hereby implied that one of the ten apostate world kingdoms fall. But in the narrower view a tenth of Jerusalem under Antichrist falls. The nine-tenths remain and become when purified the center of Christ's earthly kingdom.<div eID="gen41884" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41885" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">of men--</hi>Greek, "names of men." The men are as accurately enumerated as if their names were given.<div eID="gen41885" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41886" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">seven thousand--</hi>Elliott interprets seven chiliads or provinces, that is, the seven Dutch United Provinces lost to the papacy; and "names of men," titles of dignity, duchies, lordships, &c. Rather, seven thousand combine the two mystical perfect and comprehensive numbers seven and thousand, implying the full and complete destruction of the impenitent.<div eID="gen41886" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41887" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the remnant--</hi>consisting of the Israelite inhabitants not slain. Their conversion forms a blessed contrast to <reference osisRef="Rev.16.9">Re 16:9</reference>; and above, <reference osisRef="Rev.9.20">Re 9:20</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.9.21">21</reference>. These repenting (Zec 12:10-14; 13:<reference osisRef="1Cor.14.1">1</reference>), become in the flesh the loyal subjects of Christ reigning over the earth with His transfigured saints.<div eID="gen41887" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41888" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">gave glory to the God of heaven--</hi>which while apostates, and worshipping the beast's image, they had not done.<div eID="gen41888" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41889" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">God of heaven--</hi>The apostates of the last days, in pretended scientific enlightenment, recognize no heavenly power, but only the natural forces in the earth which come under their observation. His receiving up into heaven the two witnesses who had power during their time on earth to shut heaven from raining (<reference osisRef="Rev.11.6">Re 11:6</reference>), constrained His and their enemies who witnessed it, to acknowledge the God of heaven, to be God of the earth (<reference osisRef="Rev.11.4">Re 11:4</reference>). As in <reference osisRef="Rev.11.4">Re 11:4</reference> He declared Himself to be God of the earth by His two witnesses, so now He proves Himself to be God of heaven also. <div eID="gen41889" type="x-p"/>
entries.317b9310f6f18b7a4226f27a2aea49ca46fd2a93: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19227"/><div sID="gen41890" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19227"/><hi type="bold">14. The second woe--</hi>that under the sixth trumpet (<reference osisRef="Rev.9.12-Rev.9.21">Re 9:12-21</reference>), including also the prophecy, <reference osisRef="Rev.11.1-Rev.11.13">Re 11:1-13</reference>: Woe to the world, joy to the faithful, as their redemption draweth nigh.<div eID="gen41890" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41891" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the third woe cometh quickly--</hi>It is not mentioned in detail for the present, until first there is given a sketch of the history of the origination, suffering, and faithfulness of the Church in a time of apostasy and persecution. Instead of the third woe being detailed, the grand consummation is summarily noticed, the thanksgiving of the twenty-four elders in heaven for the establishment of Christ's kingdom on earth, attended with the destruction of the destroyers of the earth. <div eID="gen41891" type="x-p"/>
entries.8d889f9de0d4efd9a296886df0cb053b60b737ec: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19228"/><div sID="gen41892" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19228"/><hi type="bold">15. sounded--</hi>with his trumpet. Evidently "the LAST trumpet." Six is close to seven, but does not reach it. The world judgments are complete in six, but by the fulfilment of seven the world kingdoms become Christ's. Six is the number of the world given over to judgment. It is half of twelve, the Church's number, as three and a half is half of seven, the divine number for completeness. Bengel thinks the angel here to have been Gabriel, which name is compounded of El, God, and Geber, MIGHTY MAN (<reference osisRef="Rev.10.1">Re 10:1</reference>). Gabriel therefore appropriately announced to Mary the advent of the mighty God-man: compare the account of the man-child's birth which follows (<reference osisRef="Rev.12.1-Rev.12.6">Re 12:1-6</reference>), to which this forms the transition though the seventh trumpet in time is subsequent, being the consummation of the historical episode, the twelfth and thirteen chapters. The seventh trumpet, like the seventh seal and seventh vial, being the consummation, is accompanied differently from the preceding six: not the consequences which follow on earth, but those IN HEAVEN, are set before us, the great voices and thanksgiving of the twenty-four elders in heaven, as the half-hour's silence in heaven at the seventh seal, and the voice out of the temple in heaven, "It is done," at the seventh vial. This is parallel to <reference osisRef="Dan.2.44">Da 2:44</reference>, "The God of heaven shall set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break to pieces all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever." It is the setting up of Heaven's sovereignty over the earth visibly, which, when invisibly exercised, was rejected by the earthly rulers heretofore. The distinction of worldly and spiritual shall then cease. There will be no beast in opposition to the woman. Poetry, art, science, and social life will be at once worldly and Christian.<div eID="gen41892" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41893" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">kingdoms--</hi>A, B, C, and Vulgate read the singular, "The kingdom (sovereignty) of (over) the world is our Lord's and His Christ's." There is no good authority for English Version reading. The kingdoms of the world give way to the kingdom of (over) the world exercised by Christ. The earth-kingdoms are many: His shall be one. The appellation "Christ," the Anointed, is here, where His kingdom is mentioned appropriately for the first time used in Revelation. For it is equivalent to King. Though priests and prophets also were anointed, yet this term is peculiarly applied to Him as King, insomuch that "the Lord's anointed" is His title as King, in places where He is distinguished from the priests. The glorified Son of man shall rule mankind by His transfigured Church in heaven, and by His people Israel on earth: Israel shall be the priestly mediator of blessings to the whole world, realizing them first.<div eID="gen41893" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41894" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">he--</hi>not emphatic in the Greek.<div eID="gen41894" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41895" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shall reign for ever and ever--</hi>Greek, "unto the ages of the ages." Here begins the millennial reign, the consummation of "the mystery of God" (<reference osisRef="Rev.10.7">Re 10:7</reference>). <div eID="gen41895" type="x-p"/>
entries.044cdf62ab9dfa8a7306f198a7ee8bccdbfe7899: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19229"/><div sID="gen41896" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19229"/><hi type="bold">16. before God--</hi>B and Syriac read, "before the throne of God." But A, C, Vulgate, and Coptic read as English Version.<div eID="gen41896" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41897" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">seats--</hi>Greek, "thrones." <div eID="gen41897" type="x-p"/>
entries.2b9f441aa9ecc1655014a1c54e7fdc3b7315adec: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19230"/><div sID="gen41898" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19230"/><hi type="bold">17. thanks--</hi>for the answer to our prayers (<reference osisRef="Rev.6.10">Re 6:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.6.11">11</reference>) in destroying them which destroy the earth (<reference osisRef="Rev.11.18">Re 11:18</reference>), thereby preparing the way for setting up the kingdom of Thyself and Thy saints.<div eID="gen41898" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41899" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">and art to come--</hi>omitted in A, B, C, Vulgate, Syriac, Cyprian, and Andreas. The consummation having actually come, they do not address Him as they did when it was still future, "Thou that art to come." Compare <reference osisRef="Rev.11.18">Re 11:18</reference>, "is come." From the sounding of the seventh trumpet He is to His people Jah, the ever present Lord, WHO IS, more peculiarly than Jehovah "who is, was, and is to come."<div eID="gen41899" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41900" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">taken to thee thy great power--</hi>"to Thee" is not in the Greek. Christ takes to Him the kingdom as His own of right. <div eID="gen41900" type="x-p"/>
entries.d801532e5655c585a63dfd0381bf7953688f7719: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19231"/><div sID="gen41901" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19231"/><hi type="bold">18. the nations were angry--</hi>alluding to <reference osisRef="Ps.99.1">Psa 99:1</reference>, Septuagint, "The Lord is become King: let the peoples become angry." Their anger is combined with alarm (<reference osisRef="Exod.15.14">Ex 15:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Kgs.19.28">2Ki 19:28</reference>, "thy rage against Me is come up into Mine ears, I will put My hook in thy nose," &c.). Translate, as the Greek is the same. "The nations were angered, and Thy anger is come." How petty man's impotent anger, standing here side by side with that of the omnipotent God!<div eID="gen41901" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41902" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">dead ... be judged--</hi>proving that this seventh trumpet is at the end of all things, when the judgment on Christ's foes and the reward of His saints, long prayed for by His saints, shall take place.<div eID="gen41902" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41903" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the prophets--</hi>as, for instance, the two prophesying witnesses (<reference osisRef="Rev.11.3">Re 11:3</reference>), and those who have showed them kindness for Christ's sake. Jesus shall come to effect by His presence that which we have looked for long, but vainly, in His absence, and by other means.<div eID="gen41903" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41904" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">destroy them which destroy the earth--</hi>Retribution in kind (compare <reference osisRef="Rev.16.6">Re 16:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.19.27">Lu 19:27</reference>). See on <reference osisRef="Dan.7.14-Dan.7.18">Da 7:14-18</reference>. <div eID="gen41904" type="x-p"/>
entries.1d7e9d8c926d9cac642d6e141155a44acca110a7: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19232"/><div sID="gen41905" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19232"/>19. A similar solemn conclusion to that of the seventh seal, <reference osisRef="Rev.8.5">Re 8:5</reference>, and to that of the seventh vial, <reference osisRef="Rev.16.18">Re 16:18</reference>. Thus, it appears, the seven seals, the seven trumpets, and the seven vials, are not consecutive, but parallel, and ending in the same consummation. They present the unfolding of God's plans for bringing about the grand end under three different aspects, mutually complementing each other.<div eID="gen41905" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41906" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the temple--</hi>the sanctuary or Holy place (Greek, "naos"), not the whole temple (Greek, "hieron").<div eID="gen41906" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41907" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">opened in heaven--</hi>A and C read the article, "the temple of God "which is" in heaven, was opened."<div eID="gen41907" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41908" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the ark of his testament--</hi>or "... His covenant." As in the first verse the earthly sanctuary was measured, so here its heavenly antitype is laid open, and the antitype above to the ark of the covenant in the Holiest Place below is seen, the pledge of God's faithfulness to His covenant in saving His people and punishing their and His enemies. Thus this forms a fit close to the series of trumpet judgments and an introduction to the episode (the twelfth and thirteen chapters) as to His faithfulness to His Church. Here first His secret place, the heavenly sanctuary, is opened for the assurance of His people; and thence proceed His judgments in their behalf (<reference osisRef="Rev.14.15">Re 14:15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.14.17">17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.15.5">15:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.16.17">16:17</reference>), which the great company in heaven laud as "true and righteous." This then is parallel to the scene at the heavenly altar, at the close of the seals and opening of the trumpets (<reference osisRef="Rev.8.3">Re 8:3</reference>), and at the close of the episode (the twelfth through fifteenth chapters) and opening of the vials (<reference osisRef="Rev.15.7">Re 15:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.15.8">8</reference>). See on <reference osisRef="Rev.12.1">Re 12:1</reference>, note at the opening of the chapter. <chapter eID="Rev.11"/>

entries.b4904b7513024242b30648fe86ecef4b2512a3ff: <div eID="gen56238" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen56239" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen56240" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen56240" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen56239" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen56241" type="x-p"/> The command to measure the temple, <reference osisRef="Rev.11.1">Rev 11:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.11.2">Rev 11:2</reference>. The two witnesses which should prophesy twelve hundred and sixty days, <reference osisRef="Rev.11.3">Rev 11:3</reference>. The description, power, and influence of these witnesses, <reference osisRef="Rev.11.4-Rev.11.6">Rev 11:4-6</reference>. They shall be slain by the beast which shall arise out of the bottomless pit, and shall arise again after three days and a half, and ascend to heaven, <reference osisRef="Rev.11.7-Rev.11.12">Rev 11:7-12</reference>. After which shall be a great earthquake, <reference osisRef="Rev.11.13">Rev 11:13</reference>. The introduction to the third wo, <reference osisRef="Rev.11.14">Rev 11:14</reference>. The sounding of the seventh angel, and the four and twenty elders give glory to God, <reference osisRef="Rev.11.15-Rev.11.19">Rev 11:15-19</reference>. <div eID="gen56241" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56242" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen56242" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56243" type="x-p"/> And there was given me a reed - See <reference osisRef="Eze.40.3">Eze 40:3</reference>, etc. <div eID="gen56243" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56244" type="x-p"/> Measure the temple of God - This must refer to the temple of Jerusalem; and this is another presumptive evidence that it was yet standing.
entries.d3c10756d980b1f6b81106b5c9808cb8763bf7cf: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen56244" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56245" type="x-p"/> But the court - is given unto the Gentiles - The measuring of the temple probably refers to its approaching destruction, and the termination of the whole Levitical service; and this we find was to be done by the Gentiles, (Romans), who were to tread it down forty-two months; i.e., just three years and a half, or twelve hundred and sixty days. This must be a symbolical period.
entries.34061b2d7dfbb024ab7b88dc9732b2d4b0723a59: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen56245" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56246" type="x-p"/> My two witnesses - This is extremely obscure; the conjectures of interpreters are as unsatisfactory as they are endless on this point. Conjecturas conjecturis superstruunt, parum verosimiles, says Rosenmuller: quorum sententias enarrare, meum non est. I say the same. Those who wish to be amused or bewildered, may have recourse both to ancients and moderns on this subject.
entries.280c8f9d870685ef258aced228e4b153684419aa: <hi type="bold">Verse 4</hi> <div eID="gen56246" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56247" type="x-p"/> These are the two olive trees - Mentioned <reference osisRef="Zac.4.14">Zac 4:14</reference>, which there represent Zerubbabel and Joshua the high priest. The whole account seems taken from <reference osisRef="Zac.4.1-Zac.4.14">Zac 4:1-14</reference>. Whether the prophet and the apostle mean the same things by these emblems, we know not.
entries.7b4d415e44c0a2a781e480383edab50d127d6403: <hi type="bold">Verse 5</hi> <div eID="gen56247" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56248" type="x-p"/> Fire proceedeth out of their mouth - That is, they are commissioned to denounce the judgments of God against all who would attempt to prevent them from proceeding in their ministry.
entries.b2eac62de57d9dae89057dfc3cfee8c26084278c: <hi type="bold">Verse 6</hi> <div eID="gen56248" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56249" type="x-p"/> These have power to shut heaven - As Elijah did, 1 Kings 17:1-18:46. <div eID="gen56249" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56250" type="x-p"/> To turn them to blood - As Moses did, <reference osisRef="Exo.7.19-Exo.7.25">Exo 7:19-25</reference>. They shall have power to afflict the land with plagues, similar to those which were inflicted on the Egyptians.
entries.de7387450b7eb68a7ce277da9e5d0507e1a63f69: <hi type="bold">Verse 7</hi> <div eID="gen56250" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56251" type="x-p"/> The beast that ascended out of the bottomless pit - This may be what is called antichrist; some power that is opposed to genuine Christianity. But what or whence, except from the bottomless pit, i.e., under the influence and appointment of the devil, we cannot tell; nor do we know by what name this power or being should be called. The conjectures concerning the two witnesses and the beast have been sufficiently multiplied. If the whole passage, as some think, refer to the persecution raised by the Jews against the Christians, then some Jewish power or person is the beast from the bottomless pit. If it refer to the early ages of Christianity, then the beast may be one of the persecuting heathen emperors. If it refer to a later age of Christianity, then the beast may be the papal power, and the Albigenses and Waldenses the two witnesses, which were nearly extinguished by the horrible persecutions raised up against them by the Church of Rome. Whatever may be here intended, the earth has not yet covered their blood.
entries.f5bf024ad820ac5d616f0504a6804a10b9156a19: <hi type="bold">Verse 8</hi> <div eID="gen56251" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56252" type="x-p"/> The great city - Some say Rome, which may be spiritually called Sodom for its abominations, Egypt for its tyrannous cruelty, and the place where our Lord was crucified, because of its persecution of the members of Christ; but Jerusalem itself may be intended. All these things I must leave to others.
entries.6d1ff66c15cbae31fc48a2dde40479eff9176fcd: <hi type="bold">Verse 9</hi> <div eID="gen56252" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56253" type="x-p"/> Shall not suffer their dead bodies to be put in graves - They shall be treated with the greatest barbarity. Refusal of burial to the dead was allowed to be the sum of brutality and cruelty. In popish lands they will not suffer a Protestant to have Christian burial, or to have a grave in a churchyard! Contemptible wretches!
entries.6dd25d0eca36a813d45a71cf16a015bd3a4afa41: <hi type="bold">Verse 10</hi> <div eID="gen56253" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56254" type="x-p"/> Shall send gifts - This was a custom in days of public rejoicing. They sent gifts to each other, and gave portions to the poor. See <reference osisRef="Est.9.19">Est 9:19</reference>, <reference osisRef="Est.9.22">Est 9:22</reference>.
entries.6915552bd396cda8c99d41ad3d4de606b2c0feb6: <hi type="bold">Verse 11</hi> <div eID="gen56254" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56255" type="x-p"/> They stood upon their feet - Were restored to their primitive state.
