They were reckoned seven, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 1.20. here they are reduced to two; possibly it may denote the different state of God's Church. In the Old-Testament God had but one Church, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> that of the Jews; but now he hath many Churches, and they are all fed from faithful Ministers, as <ns0:hi>Olive-Branches</ns0:hi> pouring out their Oyl of Grace and Knowledg upon them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 And if any man will hurt them <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">That is, my faithful Ministers, the two Olive-branches before-mentioned, which fill the Candlesticks with Oyl.</ns0:note>, fire pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceedeth out of their mouth, and devoureth their enemies <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Here is a plain Allusion to the Stories of <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Elias,</ns0:hi> calling for Fire from Heaven; but God sheweth, that the Vi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ctory of his Ministers under the Gospel shall not be by a mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />raculous Fire called for down from Heaven (as <ns0:hi>Elias,</ns0:hi> hurt the Captains and their Bands sent to apprehend him) but by <ns0:hi>Fire out of their Mouths,</ns0:hi> according to that, Jer. 5.14. <ns0:hi>Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire, and this People wood, and it shall devour them</ns0:hi>; See also <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 1.9, 10. This also is according to <ns0:hi>Zechariah</ns0:hi>'s Vision before-mentioned, and the Revelation of the Will of God in it, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 6. <ns0:hi>Not by Might, nor by Power, but by my Spirit, saith the Lord of Hosts.</ns0:hi> The meaning is, That they shall be too hard for them, either by their faithful, lively, and powerful preaching, or by their fervent Prayers.</ns0:note>; and if any man will hurt them, he must in this manner be killed.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 These have power to shut heaven, that it rain not in the days of their prophecy <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">It is plain, that here is an Allusion to <ns0:hi>Elias,</ns0:hi> who <ns0:hi>prayed earnestly that it might not rain, and it rai<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>d not on the Earth by the space of three years and six Months,</ns0:hi> James 5.17. See the Story, 1 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 17.1. and</ns0:note>; and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 7.19.</ns0:note> have power over waters, to turn them to blood <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">to <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> who turned the Waters into Blood in <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi>;</ns0:note>, and to smite the earth with all plagues, as often as they will <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">and after was an Instrument to smite the Land of <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi> with Plagues. But what Power analogous to this the Ministers of the Gospel have had, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>r have, is not easie to determine. It is certain, the Apostles had a miraculous Power, but they rarely used it, but in do<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing good to Men; <ns0:hi>Ananias</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Saphira</ns0:hi> indeed were struck dead upon their Word, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 5. and <ns0:hi>Elymas</ns0:hi> the Sorcerer was <ns0:hi>struck blind</ns0:hi> by them; but this Power is long since ceased. Mr. <ns0:hi>Mede</ns0:hi> understands this Power of the <ns0:hi>Keys</ns0:hi> of Doctrine, and <ns0:hi>Church-censures</ns0:hi> the Ministers of the Gospel should be intrusted with; so as they should not preach the Gospel unto such as contemned their Ministry, by the withholding of which means of Grace, also they would be deprived of the Dew of heavenly Grace. And, indeed, this seemeth more proper than to understand it of the <ns0:hi>Keys of Discipline</ns0:hi>; for what Power of this Nature have Ministers over those who are without? I take a general Explication to be the best. If any hurt them, God shall revenge their Cause, not only by spiritual, but by temporal Judgments, bringing all man<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ner of Evils upon their Adversaries. They are said to have Power to do it, because God will do it in the Revenge of the Injuries done unto them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 And when they shall have finished their testimony <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">'<ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>; Mr. <ns0:hi>Mede</ns0:hi> notes, that this is ill translated by the <ns0:hi>Pr<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>terperfect Tense</ns0:hi>: the true English of it is, when they shall be about to finish their Testimony: When they have prophesied in Sackcloth the most of their twelve hundred and sixty years, they shall meet with <ns0:hi>ultimum conatum Anti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />christi,</ns0:hi> the last Struggle of the Beast for life.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 17.8.</ns0:note> the beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">That is, the <ns0:hi>Beast</ns0:hi> mentioned, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 13.1, 4. (by which the <ns0:hi>Papacy</ns0:hi> is meant whom they have plagued all the time of their Prophecy, tho continual Sufferers from it) shall get life again, and make one push more, possibly the sharpest yet made,</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Dan. 7.21. Zech. 14.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> shall make war against them <ns0:hi>u,</ns0:hi> and shall overcome them, and kill them <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">and be too hard for them, and kill them. It is a great Question; Whether this be to be understood of taking away their na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tural Lives, or of a <ns0:hi>c<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>v<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>l Death</ns0:hi> relating to them as <ns0:hi>Witnesses,</ns0:hi> making them as if they were naturally dead. The latter of these seemeth to me, much the more probable, for these Rea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons; 1. Supposing the godly Magistracy, or Ministry, or the latter alone, to be the <ns0:hi>two Witnesses,</ns0:hi> it doth not seem pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bable that ever the <ns0:hi>Papacy</ns0:hi> shall so far prevail, as to kill all such over the face of the whole Church. 2. Neither is the Holy Ghost here speaking of them as Men, but as <ns0:hi>Witnesses.</ns0:hi> 3. Nor would either Friends, or Enemies suffer dead Bodies to be unburied three days and an half, in the Street of a great City, as <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 8, 9. 4. Neither is their Resurrection men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tioned, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 11. to be understood of a corporal Resurrection. I take therefore the killing here mentioned, to be understood of a destroying them as Witnesses, turning Magistrates out of their Places, and Ministers out of their Places, tho it be not probable that such a Malice and Hatred as should cause this, should terminate without the Blood of some of them; but that surely is not the thing principally here intended.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 And their dead bodies <ns0:hi>shall lie</ns0:hi> in the street of <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 17.1, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> the great city, which spiritually is called So<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom and Egypt <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Their Bodies dead, in the sense before-mentioned, shall continue so for <ns0:hi>three days and an half</ns0:hi> (of which we shall speak, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 11.) But what is here meant, 1. by the <ns0:hi>great City</ns0:hi>? 2. By the <ns0:hi>Street of the great City</ns0:hi>? Some, by the great City, would have <ns0:hi>Hierusalem</ns0:hi> understood; but that was now far from a great City, nor do the Addition of those words in the lat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter end of the Verse prove it; for Christ was not crucified in that City, but without the Gates. Most judicious Interpre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ters, by the <ns0:hi>great City,</ns0:hi> here understand <ns0:hi>Rome,</ns0:hi> which is seven or eight times (under the name of <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi>) so called in this Book, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 14.8. and <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 16.19. & 18.10, 10, 18, 19, 21. nor is any other City but that so called. This great City is here said in a spiritual Sense, to be <ns0:hi>Sodom</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Egypt; Sodom</ns0:hi> for Whoredom and Filthiness; <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> for Ooppression of the Lord's <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi> As to the second Question, what is here meant by <ns0:hi>the Street of the great City?</ns0:hi> Mr. <ns0:hi>Mede</ns0:hi> hath irrefragably pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ved, that it cannot be meant of any <ns0:hi>Parish,</ns0:hi> or such place in this City, as we call a <ns0:hi>Street.</ns0:hi> 1. Because our <ns0:hi>Lord was crucified</ns0:hi> neither in any Street, or Parish, or any other place within the Walls of <ns0:hi>Hierusalem.</ns0:hi> 2. Both <ns0:hi>Hierusalem</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Rome</ns0:hi> had many more than one Street. 3. Because the Bodies be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing dead, doubtless lay in the place where they were slain; but Men do not use to fight in the Streets of Cities. 4. Nor was that a Place for all People, Kindred, Tongues, and Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions, to see them in. He therefore rightly judgeth, that the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> word which we translate a <ns0:hi>Street,</ns0:hi> signifies the Terri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tories and Jurisdiction of this City. See what he saies to justifie this in his <ns0:hi>Clavis Apocal.</ns0:hi> 40. <ns0:hi>p.</ns0:hi> 138.</ns0:note>, where also our Lord was cru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cified <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">And this makes the last clause plain; for tho our Lord was not crucified within any City, or in the Street of any City, yet he was cru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cified in a place belonging to the Jurisdiction of the <ns0:hi>Roman Emperor</ns0:hi>; and it is very likely that it is in <ns0:hi>Europe</ns0:hi> that the <ns0:hi>Witnesses</ns0:hi> shall be slain, which, in this Sense, was all of it a <ns0:hi>Street</ns0:hi> belonging to the City of <ns0:hi>Rome.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:611" />9 And they of the people, and kindreds, and tongues, and nations <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">That is, a Multitude of People of all sorts shall take notice of this Suppression of these two Witnesses in their bearing witness for God, and all the cruel dealings with them.</ns0:note>, shall see their dead bo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dies three days and an half <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">There are great Disputes what time these three days and an half denote; it cannot be understood of three natural, or artificial days: for (as it is noted by the most judicious In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terpreters) this is much too short a time for all People to see their dead Bodies, to rejoice over them, and to make merry, and to send Presents one to another in Testification of the Satisfaction of their Lusts, upon the Victory got over them. I find some understand these three days and an half, of the 1260 years, wherein they prophesied in Sackcloth, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 3. which they thus make out; they first conclude, that these are prophetical days, and so signifie three years and an half; then they resolve each of those years into days, and count 3 times 360 days; (for in those Countries they say the Year was counted to contain but 360 days) to which they add 180, the half of 360, for the half day, which make up 1260 days, or 42 months; which is the just time both of the Beasts Reign, and of the Womans abode in the Wilder<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness, and of the Witnesses Prophesying in Sack-cloth, and of the Gentiles treading down the outward Court; but it seems very hard, thus first to make the three days three years in a Prophetical sense, and then again to resolve those years into days, and make those days so many more years; this looks as much like Oppression to the Text, as the counting Interest upon Interest to a Debtor. 2. It plain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly confounds the time of the Prophecying of the Witnes<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ses in Sack-cloth, with the time of their lying dead. Now although the time of their lying dead must be within the 1260 days, in the latter end thereof (for it must be with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />in the Beasts 42 months, mentioned <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 13.5.) yet it seems hard to make it as long as the Beasts Reign. It certainly signifies a time toward the end of the Beasts Reign, when there shall be a more eminent and universal suppression of the faithful Witnesses of Christ than ever was before: It seemeth therefore rather to be understood more gene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rally for a short time; as much such a phrase or way of speaking is used, <ns0:hi>Hosea</ns0:hi> 6.2. or else for a determinate time of such three years and an half as we ordinarily count. I must confess the <ns0:hi>half day</ns0:hi> being added, makes me more inclined to the latter; for though it be usual with us to express a short time by <ns0:hi>two or three days,</ns0:hi> and this seems by that Text of <ns0:hi>Hosea</ns0:hi> to have been an ancient way of speak<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, yet we do not use to put in <ns0:hi>half days</ns0:hi> when we so speak. I do therefore agree with those who think the time here specified is, to be understood of three ordinary years and an half; and the rather, because this is the ve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry time that Christ was under the power of the <ns0:hi>Pharisees.</ns0:hi> As three days (that is, part of them) was the time of his being under the power of Death; so three years and an half was the just time of all the indignity that he suffer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed from his manifestation to the World, to his Death. And (as we read in the 1 <ns0:hi>Ma<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>hah.</ns0:hi>) it was the just time of <ns0:hi>Anti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ochus</ns0:hi> his oppressing of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> whom Divines judge that <ns0:hi>Daniel</ns0:hi> in his 11th Chapter makes a Type of Antichrist.</ns0:note>, and shall not suffer their dead bodies to be put in graves <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Divines are divided whether these words be to be un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstood of Enemies or Friends. If it be to be understood of Friends, the Death being a civil Death, principally that was spoken of, it signifieth the Providence of God so work<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing for his <ns0:hi>Witnesses,</ns0:hi> by the adherence of a party to them, that their Adversaries the <ns0:hi>Popish</ns0:hi> party should not wholly extinguish them, which hath been seen all along the Story of the Church; though their Adversaries have been war<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ring against them, overcome and kill'd them, yet they have not been able to bury them; nor shall they be able to do it at this last pinch, when they shall have a greater Victo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry over them than ever before, and <ns0:hi>kill them</ns0:hi> to a further degree. But methinks the phrase rather signifies this, an act of Enemies, who to shew their further malice to them, and contempt and scorn of them, are said to be so inhu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mane, as not to suffer their dead Bodies to be buried.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 And they that dwell upon the earth <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">It is plain by the repeating of the same words in the close of the Verse, that by those that <ns0:hi>dwell upon the earth</ns0:hi> are meant <ns0:hi>earthly carnal Men,</ns0:hi> whether <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Atheists</ns0:hi>; Men that are mad upon their Lusts; for these are those in whose Consciences faithful and powerful Preaching breeds a torment and uneasiness, so as they always count Godly Ministers their Enemies (as <ns0:hi>Ahab</ns0:hi> told <ns0:hi>Elijah</ns0:hi>) and are not able to <ns0:hi>bear their Words</ns0:hi> (as the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> could not bear the words of <ns0:hi>Amos.</ns0:hi>)</ns0:note> shall rejoice over them, and make merry, and shall send gifts one to another <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">These therefore shall keep Holiday, when they see these their Enemies conquered, and shew all signs and expressions of Joy. These Preachers were they that hindred them from a quiet sleep in their Beds of Lusts,</ns0:note>, because these two pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets tormented them that dwelt upon the earth <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">And though they fought against them only with a Fire going out of their Mouths, as Prophets declaring the Will of God to be contrary to their lewd practices, and denoun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cing God's Wrath against those that did such things; yet their Preaching made their Heads ake, partly by alarming their Consciences so as they often flew in their faces; and by it they were exposed to the reproach of People, as li<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving directly contrary to the Divine Rule, and in defiance of his Law; thus they <ns0:hi>torment</ns0:hi> wicked Men, who therefore always did, and always will triumph in their suppression, or in any evil that shall betide them. And as they see their suppres<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sion greater than ever before, (as it will be undoubtedly during these three years and an half,) so the Triumph of lewd and wicked Men will be proportionably more, tho it will be but like a Widows Joy for a short time, for it will appear that their dead Bodies were not put into the Grave.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 And after three days and an half <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">After that short time which God had determined for <ns0:hi>Antichrist</ns0:hi> (just before his time should be expired) or after the precise time of forty two months, or three years and an half was expired, when the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> thought they had fully prevailed, and should be no more troubled with <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi>'s <ns0:hi>Witnesses.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, the Spirit of life from God entred into them, and they stood upon their feet <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">God who alone can quicken the dead, reviveth them, and restoreth them again to their employment as his Prophets; for it is plain this cannot be understood of a corporal Resurrection; for 1. Their Death was not of that nature; nor, 2. Doth the Scripture give us any hints of any such Resurrection before the coming of Christ to the last Judgment.</ns0:note>, and great fear fell upon them which saw them <ns0:hi>h.</ns0:hi>
                  <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">This strikes a great fear into all their Ene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mies, amazed to think what God was about to do, and rightly pre<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>aging this would be their ruine.</ns0:note>
                  <ns0:note place="bottom">It is a great question now, whether the time here spo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken of for slaying the Witnesses, and their rising again, be past, or yet to come. I must confess the <ns0:hi>Papacy</ns0:hi> had got such a Victory over the faithful Witnesses of Christ for some Ages before the <ns0:hi>Reformation</ns0:hi> began in <ns0:hi>Germany</ns0:hi> about 1517, and there was so sudden a resurrection of them in the first Reformers brought to pass, and carried on by such a stu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pendious series of Providences, that I cannot wonder that some did think the time past: But we who have out-lived that time more than 150 years, seeing the <ns0:hi>Turks</ns0:hi> (whom all judicious Interpreters make the four Angels bound by the River <ns0:hi>Euphrates</ns0:hi> loosed) still so rampant; and the Papacy still so predominant, and daily treading down the outward Court, have no reason to judg the <ns0:hi>slaying of the Witnesses</ns0:hi> yet over, at least that they are yet risen, and standing upon their Feet; or that the <ns0:hi>seventh Angel</ns0:hi> hath yet sounded; but that we are as yet under the period of time signified by the sounding of the <ns0:hi>sixth Trumpet</ns0:hi>; and to expect a further degree of this Evening before it will be Light over the Universal Church, (for we must not think any particular Church intended here,) and this appears most probable al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />so from what followeth before the sounding of the seventh Angel, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 15.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 And they <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">That is the two Witnesses so often before spoken of.</ns0:note> heard a great voice from hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven, saying unto them, Come up hither <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Heard God by a singular <ns0:hi>Providence</ns0:hi> calling them again to their former work and station in his Church; or (a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> some) to an higher, and more famous place in his Church than they formerly enjoyed; for by <ns0:hi>Heaven</ns0:hi> the most and best Interpreters understand the Church, as it often signifies in this Book.</ns0:note>, And they ascended up to heaven in a cloud, and their enemies beheld them <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">And this was done in the face of their Ene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mies. In this sense of this Verse I find the generality of judicious Interpreters agreed.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:611" />13 And the same hour <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">That is, about the same time, when the Spirit of Life from God entred into the Witnesses, and they were again restored.</ns0:note> was there a great earthquake <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">By Earthquake doubtless is here meant a great confusion in the World, and shaking of Nations by Differen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces one with another, and Wars; see the Notes on <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 6.12. By the City is doubtless meant the great City before named, spiritually called <ns0:hi>Sodom</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> elsewhere <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi>; by which <ns0:hi>Rome</ns0:hi> is to be understood. What is meant by the tenth part of it falling, is not so well agreed; some by it understanding many Kingdoms fallen off from its Jurisdicti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on: Others a great part of its Tribute or Dominion.</ns0:note>, and the tenth part of the city fell <ns0:hi>p,</ns0:hi> and in the earthquake were slain <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Gr. <ns0:hi>Names of men.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> of men seven thousand <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">These words seem to intimate that the restauration of the Witnes<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ses shall not be without opposition, and that the opposition shall not be great, 7000 is a small number to fall in such a quarrel: but the <ns0:hi>Papal</ns0:hi> party shall appear to have cheat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed the World so with their Impostures, and so to have im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />posed upon them, that the World shall grow sick of them, and when the time comes for God to put a final period to them, the number shall be but few that adventure for them.</ns0:note>; and the remnant were affrighted <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Others shall be affrighted, either from their own Consci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ences, or from the stupendous Dispensations of Divine Provi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dence in the fall of the great City.</ns0:note>, and gave glory to the God of heaven <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">And give Glory to God, by confessing their Er<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ors, and turning to an ingenu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ous and sincere acknowledgment of the Truth, Instead of worshipping Saints and Angels and Images, worshipping the True and Living God of Heaven and Earth only.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 8.13. & 9.12. & 15.1</ns0:note> The second wo is past <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">That is, here endeth the misery that is like to come upon the World in that period of time which shall follow the sounding of the Sixth Trumpet.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> behold, the third wo cometh quickly <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">The third Woe sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifies those Calamities which should come in that period of time prophesied of by the sounding of the seventh Trum<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pets, this makes a late learned Author think that all that which went before, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> The Gentiles treading down the outward Court, the slaying of the Witnesses, and their re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />suscitation must be under the sixth Trumpet, which Period endeth not until the Churches Enemies be ready to be de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stroyed; whose Destruction is afterwards opened to us in the Angels pouring out their Viols.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 And the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 10.7.</ns0:note> seventh angel sounded <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">The last of those Angels mentioned <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 8.2.</ns0:note>, and there were great voices in heaven, saying <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">St. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> in his Vision heard great acclamations and shoutings for the Victory which Christ and his Gospel had got over the Beast.</ns0:note>, The kingdoms of this world are become <ns0:note n="†" place="bottom">Chap. 12.10.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:hi>the kingdoms</ns0:hi> of our Lord, and of his Christ, and he shall reign for ever and ever <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:p>So that a great part of the World, casting off the <ns0:hi>Papacy</ns0:hi> that new <ns0:hi>Gentilism,</ns0:hi> together with all their abo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />minable Idolatries and Superstitions, embraced the truth of the Gospel. Here ariseth a great Question, whether the seven Vials, of which we shall find the sixteenth Chapter treating, do belong all to the <ns0:hi>seventh Trumpet,</ns0:hi> or some of them belong to the sixth Trumpet, of which mention hath been before made. Great Divines are on both sides as to this Question, Mr. <ns0:hi>Pool</ns0:hi> in his Latine <ns0:hi>Synopsis</ns0:hi> hath collected together their reasons, of which I shall give a short ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />count, leaving my Reader for a fuller satisfaction to the La<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tin <ns0:hi>Synopsis.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p>Those who think that the seven Vials do all relate to the seventh Trumpet, and contemporize with it, in defence of their Opinion say,
<ns0:list>
                           <ns0:item>1. That the seven Seals, and the seven Trumpets, and the seven Vials, are all mentioned in the same form of speech, and therefore the seven Vials are not to be divided, some to one Trumpet, some to another.</ns0:item>
                           <ns0:item>2. Because the seventh Trumpet and the seven Vials are one and the same thing, nothing being revealed under the seven Vials which doth not belong so the seventh Trumpet; they agree in their Titles of <ns0:hi>Woes,</ns0:hi> in the nature of the Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />velations, in their Objects, both the one and other de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />claring the ruine of Antichrist; both of them are mention<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed as the last Plagues to come upon the World before the Last Day.</ns0:item>
                           <ns0:item>3. All the Vials are of the same nature, declaring but the Judgments by which God setting up the Kingdom of Christ, would ruine Antichrist, they only differ in the degrees of the Plagues, each one rising higher than the other.</ns0:item>
                           <ns0:item>4. The seventh Trumpet cannot declare the ruine of An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tichrist, unless the seven Vials be poured out under it, for they shew the means by which he must be destroyed.</ns0:item>
                           <ns0:item>5. The seventh Trumpet soundeth immediately upon the slaying of the Witnesses, and contemporizeth with the whole course of their renewed Liberty, and therefore the Period signified by it, must be before the Fall of Antichrist decla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />red by the sixth Vial.</ns0:item>
                           <ns0:item>5. The seventh Trumpet soundeth immediately after the expiration of the 1260 days; before the end of which none of the Vials were poured out.</ns0:item>
                        </ns0:list>
                     </ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p>Those who think that diverse of the Vials were poured out, or shall be poured out before the sounding of this seventh Trumpet say,</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p>That the Beasts Kingdom beginning to fall under the <ns0:hi>sixth Trumpet,</ns0:hi> several of the <ns0:hi>Vials,</ns0:hi> declaring the degrees of his fal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ling, must belong to that. It appeareth by all we have in this Chapter from <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 7. to 15. that Antichrist's Kingdom was in a great measure weakned under the sixth Trumpet, particularly from <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 11. to 13. To which those who think that all the <ns0:hi>Vials</ns0:hi> related to the seventh Trumpet say, That they grant that there were some preparations to the final ruine of Antichrist, during the period of the <ns0:hi>sixth Trumpet,</ns0:hi> but the seven Vials signify the further progress and perfecti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on of his ruine, which falls under the period signified by the seventh Trumpet; this being premised, I proceed with the Text.</ns0:p>
                  </ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">It is doubted here whether those words, <ns0:hi>are become the Kingdoms of the Lord and his Christ,</ns0:hi> be to be un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstood as being actually so, or now beginning to be so. Those who make the sense that they now actually were so, must understand the time to be the Day of Judgment, or some time next to it, and consequently must think that five at least of the seven Vials, mentioned <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 10. belonged to the sixth Trumpet. Those who make the sense, <ns0:hi>are begin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ning to become the Kingdoms of the Lord,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>shall shortly be so,</ns0:hi> may make all the seven Vials to belong to the seventh Trum<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pet; by becoming the Kingdoms of the Lord Christ, he means in outward Profession: So as Antichrist shall reign no more, but they shall be ruled by the Officers of the Lord Christ, until they be taken up to reign with him in Glory.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 And the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 4.4. and 5.8.</ns0:note> four and twenty elders which sat before God on their seats, fell upon their faces, and worshipped God <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">I take this to signify no more than the Triumph of the Saints and Angels in Heaven upon this Victory of the Lord over Antichrist, and the promoval of Christ's Kingdom; and certainly if there be Joy in Heaven upon the Conversi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on of <ns0:hi>one Sinner,</ns0:hi> as we are told <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 15.7. we must imagine a much greater Joy upon the Conversion of Nations and King<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />doms unto Christ.</ns0:note>,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 Saying, we give thee thanks, O Lord God Almighty, which art, and wast, and art to come <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">It is a <ns0:hi>phrase</ns0:hi> denoting God's <ns0:hi>Eternity</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Immutability,</ns0:hi> we met with it before, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 4.8.</ns0:note>, because thou hast taken to thee thy great power, and hast reigned <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Those Coelestial Beings bless God for exerting his Power, and recovering the King<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom of Christ out of the hands of Antichrist, and setting his King upon his holy Hill of <ns0:hi>Zion.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 And the nations were angry <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Those who have not been of thy true <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi>; but old or modern Gentiles, they have been angry long enough.</ns0:note>, and thy wrath is come <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Now it is time for thee to shew thy self angry, and thou hast begun to do it.</ns0:note>, and the time of the dead that they should be judged <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The time is come for thee to judg the cause of thy faithful Witnesses, and all those who have died in testimony to thy Truth.</ns0:note>, and that thou shouldst give reward unto thy servants the prophets <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">And for thee to reward such as have faithfully revealed thy Will.</ns0:note>, and to the saints <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">And not only them; but all thy Holy Ones.</ns0:note>, and them that fear thy name, small and great <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Without respect to their Quality in the World, be they little or great.</ns0:note>, and shouldst destroy them which <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>corrupt.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> destroy the earth <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">The time also is come, when thou hast destroyed, or wilt destroy that Antichristian Brood, which so long hath plagued the Earth, and destroyed thy People in it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 15.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> the temple of God <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Some hereby the <ns0:hi>Temple of God,</ns0:hi> understand the repre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sentation of the <ns0:hi>Temple</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Hierusalem</ns0:hi>; others understand the <ns0:hi>Church Triumphant</ns0:hi>; others the Church of Christ militant here upon Earth.</ns0:note> was opened in heaven <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Accordingly by <ns0:hi>Heaven</ns0:hi> they understand ei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther the natural Heavens, or the Christian Church; it seem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth to be a plain allusion to the <ns0:hi>Iewish Church,</ns0:hi> whose <ns0:hi>Temple</ns0:hi> was ordinarily shut up in the time of Wicked and Idolatrous Princes, who regarded not the true Worship of God; so as all the time of <ns0:hi>Soul</ns0:hi>'s Reign the Ark abode in the private House of <ns0:hi>Obed Ed<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:hi>; and when <ns0:hi>Iosiah</ns0:hi> came to Reign, he sound the <ns0:hi>Temple</ns0:hi> neglected all the days of his Father <ns0:hi>Am<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>n,</ns0:hi> and Grandfather <ns0:hi>Ma<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>asses,</ns0:hi> and the Book of the Law in the Rubbish. But when good Princes came to the Throne, such as <ns0:hi>Hezekiah</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iosiah,</ns0:hi> they opened the <ns0:hi>Temple,</ns0:hi> restoring the true Worship of God: So under the <ns0:hi>New-Testament,</ns0:hi> during the whole Reign of <ns0:hi>Antichrist,</ns0:hi> where he prevails, Idolatry and Superstition obtain, and the true Worship of God is supprest: but his time being now expiring, God sheweth <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> that there shall be a restoring of the true Worship of God, and a Liberty both to Ministers and People to worship God ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to his Will. For tho <ns0:hi>Antichrist</ns0:hi> was not yet wholly destroyed, nor his Party extinguished, yet he had lost his Power and Dominion, and God was now beginning to reckon with him for the Blood of his Saints, which was all to be done before all the Kingdoms of the World should be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />come the Kingdoms of the Lord Christ.</ns0:note>, and there was seen in his temple the ark of his Testament <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">In the Temple of old, the Ark of the Covenant was the great Symbol of God's Presence; hence God is said to have dwelt betwixt the <ns0:hi>Cherubims.</ns0:hi> In the Ark were the <ns0:hi>two Tables</ns0:hi> of the Law; so as this Phrase may either note the pure, free, and ordina<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry expounding of the Law of God, which should be upon the Down-fall of <ns0:hi>Antichrist</ns0:hi>; or the Presence of God with his Church in that more pure and reformed state.</ns0:note>: and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 16.18.</ns0:note> there were light<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nings, and voices, and thundrings, and an earth<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quake, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 16.21.</ns0:note> great hail <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:p>But such a Work of Providence being not like to be effected without the Ruine of Antichrist, God sheweth it shall be ushered in with <ns0:hi>Lightnings,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Voices,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Thunderings,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>great Hail</ns0:hi>; by terrible things in Righteousness (as the <ns0:hi>Psalmist</ns0:hi> speaketh.) The Consequents of which, were the seven <ns0:hi>Vials,</ns0:hi> of which we shall read, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 16. pouring out Plagues upon the <ns0:hi>Anti-christian</ns0:hi> Party, until they should be wholly rooted out, and Christ alone should be exalted in his Church, and rule as King upon his holy Hill of <ns0:hi>Zion.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p>From this mysterious Portion of holy Writ thus opened, it appeareth that God, in these foregoing Chapters, hath (tho more summarily) instructed his Prophet in what should come to pass to the final Ruine of the <ns0:hi>Roman Empire,</ns0:hi> (considered as <ns0:hi>Pagan,</ns0:hi> that is, till <ns0:hi>Constantine</ns0:hi>'s time) and also of the Reign of <ns0:hi>Antichrist.</ns0:hi> From whence it must needs follow, that whatsoever followeth this Chapter, and cannot be applied to the time of Christ's Kingdom, must contem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />porize with something which went before, and belong to some Period comprehended under the Vision of the Seals, or of the Trumpets. The three next Chapters are judged to relate wholly to things past, God therein representing to his Prophet the state of his Church (as some think) from the Nativity of Christ, however, from his time, during the whole time that <ns0:hi>Rome</ns0:hi> continued <ns0:hi>Pagan,</ns0:hi> or should continue <ns0:hi>Antichristian.</ns0:hi> The following Chapters shewing the gradual De<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />struction of <ns0:hi>Antichrist</ns0:hi> by the seven last Plagues.</ns0:p>
